newsitem.title: USA: KPMG says it told Mercury of problems during audit.
newsitem.headline: KPMG says it told Mercury of problems during audit.

text.p: KPMG Peat Marwick LLP responded to being replaced Tuesday as Mercury Finance Co's auditor by saying it had discovered Mercury's financial irregularities during its audit of the 1996 statement and immediately brought them to the company's attention.
KMPG said it was disappointed with Mercury's decision to replace it as auditor.
Mercury on Tuesday replaced KPMG with Arthur Andersen LLP.
KMPG said that Mercury issued a news release on January 23 about its 1996 earnings over the objections of KMPG, which had not yet completed the audit.
Mercury last month restated its earnings over the past four years, lowering them by about $90 million, and blamed its controller, whom it fired.
The controller's attorney said Mercury was engaging in a charade and that James Doyle - the former controller, was cooperating with Federal authorities.
Mercury Finance was not immediately available for comment.
